settings.updates.title: Updates
settings.updates.status.idle: Kento looks for a new version shortly after it starts.
settings.updates.status.waiting: Kento {version} is downloaded and verified. New jobs can start again after the restart that installs it.
settings.updates.status.restarting: Kento restarts in a few seconds to install version {version}.
settings.updates.waiting.jobs: {count, plural, one {Waiting for # job to finish.} other {Waiting for # jobs to finish.}}
settings.updates.waiting.paused: Jobs are paused: resume them so the update can install.
settings.updates.waiting.editing: Waiting for the open panel in Kento’s window to close, so nothing you are working on is lost.
settings.updates.waiting.installs: Waiting for the tool download to finish.
settings.updates.failed.offline: Kento could not reach GitHub. It works on as before and tries again in an hour.
settings.updates.failed.signature: The downloaded update did not pass the signature check, so it was not used. Kento tries again in an hour.
settings.updates.failed.install: The update could not be installed; this version keeps working. Kento tries again in an hour.
settings.updates.failed.other: Looking for updates did not work this time. Kento tries again in an hour.
settings.updates.policy: Updates are not optional, and no version can be skipped. Kento looks for a new version shortly after it starts and every 6 hours, downloads it in the background and checks its signature. Running and waiting jobs then finish, Kento says it is restarting, and it installs the update.
settings.updates.shortcut: {shortcut} looks for a new version at once, from any Kento window.
settings.updates.locked: Kento may not change the folder it is in, so installing an update asks for an administrator’s password. Choose Update and restart when a new version is ready.
settings.updates.translocated: macOS runs this copy from a temporary, read-only place because it was opened where it was downloaded, so it cannot update itself. Move Kento to the Applications folder and open it from there.
settings.updates.development: This is a development build, which never installs updates. New versions are on the release page.
settings.privacy.title: Privacy
settings.privacy.text: Kento works on your computer. Files are never uploaded, and there is no account, analytics or telemetry. Kento goes online only when you download tools or media, and to check for updates: every few hours it reads the small latest.json file from Kento’s releases on GitHub, and sends nothing about you or your files.

setup.title: Tool setup
setup.text: Kento converts images, PDFs, archives and text on its own. Video, audio and office files need free tools that Kento downloads once.
setup.privacy: Downloads come from the tools’ own builds and are checked against a fixed fingerprint before they run. Kento goes online only when you start a download.

editor.redact.eraseHint: Fills the area in from what is around it: for your own logo, a date stamp or a small mark.
editor.vertical.window: 9:16 window, {width} × {height} at {x}; the arrow keys move it
editor.vertical.cropHint: Drag the window sideways on the picture to choose what stays.
editor.vertical.blurHint: The whole picture across the width, over a blurred, darker copy of itself.
editor.vertical.colorHint: The whole picture across the width, over a plain color.
editor.vertical.whole: The whole video. To use a part of it, set its start and end with I and O.

editor.rotate.now.left: A quarter turn to the left
editor.rotate.hint: Mirror swaps left and right; flip turns the picture upside down.
editor.rotate.same: These cancel each other out: the picture stays as it is.
editor.rotate.keep: The sound and the format stay as they are.
editor.loop.reverseHint: From the end back to the start, the sound too.
editor.loop.boomerangHint: Forwards, then backwards, as many times as you choose.
editor.loop.repeatHint: The clip again and again, with its sound.
editor.loop.slow: Long videos take a while: Kento reverses them a few seconds at a time.
editor.color.hint: The picture shows the result as you change it; the look comes first, then the sliders.
editor.stabilize.text: Kento first follows how the camera moves through the whole video, then smooths that movement and zooms in a little, so the moving edges stay out of sight.
editor.stabilize.time: This takes longer than the video itself plays.
editor.normalize.text: Kento measures the loudness first, then adjusts it in a second pass (EBU R128).

editor.channels.hint: How loud each channel will be. Mono mixes both into one; stereo plays the same sound on both.

editor.cut.result: The result lasts {length}; {removed} is cut out.

editor.music.silentVideo: This video has no sound; the music becomes its sound.
editor.music.duck: Lower the music while someone speaks

editor.music.hint: The music fades in at the start and out at the end of the video. The preview plays it with the video.

editor.denoise.preview: The preview plays the file as it is; you hear the change in the saved file.

settings.tools.title: Tools
settings.tools.note: Kento uses a tool it finds on this computer before its own download. A program you choose must be FFmpeg 6, yt-dlp 2025.11.12, Deno 2.3, LibreOffice 7 or ExifTool 12, or newer.

toolchain.failed.remove: The tools are in use. Try again when the running jobs have finished.

error.codec.libreoffice: This needs LibreOffice from the Office tools. Open Home and choose Complete setup.

error.codec.ytdlp: Downloading from the web needs the media tools (yt-dlp and Deno). Open Home and choose Complete setup.
error.codec.background: Removing backgrounds needs the Extras tools (ONNX Runtime and the background-removal model). Open Home and choose Complete setup.

automation.paused: Paused: no rule watches its folder until you resume.
automation.empty.title: No rules yet
automation.empty.text: A rule watches a folder and handles every new file that lands in it: it converts the file, runs a recipe or a tool on it, or moves it.
automation.empty.example: For example: PNGs that land in Screenshots become WEBP files in Optimized.
automation.warning.inside: The output folder is inside the watched folder. Kento never handles its own results again, but the folders are easier to follow apart.
automation.field.name: Name
automation.field.extensionsHint: For example png, jpg. Empty: every file.
automation.field.patternHint: * stands for any text and ? for one character, as in Screenshot*.
automation.field.noRecipes: No recipes yet: make one under Recipes first.

cli.help:
Kento on the command line: converts and compresses files on this computer.

Usage:
  kento convert FILES… --to FORMAT [--out FOLDER]
  kento tool TOOL FILES… [options] [--out FOLDER]
  kento recipe list
  kento recipe run RECIPE FILES… [--out FOLDER]
  kento formats
  kento routes FORMAT
  kento help COMMAND

Options:
  --json          prints the result as one JSON document
  -q, --quiet     shows no progress
  -h, --help      shows help
  -V, --version   shows the version

Results go next to each file, or into the --out folder. Kento never overwrites a file.

Exit codes: 0 done, 1 a job failed, 2 wrong usage, 3 not possible, 4 a tool is missing, 130 cancelled.
cli.help.convert:
Converts files to another format, one result per file.

Usage: kento convert FILES… --to FORMAT [--out FOLDER]

  --to FORMAT        the format to make: jpg, pdf, mp3… (kento formats lists them)
  -o, --out FOLDER   writes the results into this folder

Example: kento convert photo.heic --to jpg
cli.help.tool:
Runs a tool on files.

Usage: kento tool TOOL FILES… [options] [--out FOLDER]

Tools:
{tools}

compress: --quality 1–100, --ratio 5–95 (the result as a percentage of the original size) or --target-size SIZE (25MB, 800KB); quality 75 without one.
denoise: --strength light|medium|strong (medium without one); --rumble also takes away the lowest hum and rumble.
remove-pauses: --threshold DB, how quiet a pause is (-80 to -10, -40 without one); --min-length SECONDS, the shortest pause (0.6); --keep SECONDS of each pause left on both sides (0.15).
stabilize: --strength light|medium|strong (medium without one).
rotate-video: --turn right|left|half, --mirror (left to right) and --flip (upside down); at least one of them.
merge-video: the videos in the order given, with a cut between them, or --transition fade|fade-black|slide|wipe, each --seconds 0.2–2 long (0.5 without it).
merge-audio: the files in the order given; --crossfade SECONDS, 0–10 (none without it).
images-to-pdf: --page fit|a4|letter and --margin MILLIMETRES.
read-qr: prints the codes; --format txt|csv|json saves them as a report.

The other tools need choices made in Kento’s window.

Examples:
  kento tool compress video.mp4 --target-size 25MB
  kento tool merge-video a.mp4 b.mp4 --transition fade --seconds 1
cli.help.recipe:
Runs your recipes: steps saved under a name in Kento.

Usage:
  kento recipe list
  kento recipe run RECIPE FILES… [--out FOLDER]

RECIPE is a recipe’s name or id. Each file gets its own result, named after the recipe: photo - Instagram.jpg.

Example: kento recipe run Instagram photo.jpg
cli.help.formats:
Lists the formats Kento reads and writes, with what each converts to.

Usage: kento formats [--json]
cli.help.routes:
Shows what a format converts to, what converts to it, and which tools that needs.

Usage: kento routes FORMAT

Example: kento routes heic
